details:
Another form of https://feedback.vrchat.com/udon/p/toggling-vertex-color-always-in-gamma-color-space-causes-inconsistent-ui-brightn

The lost `_Tint` in that report is the same runtime swap. Here it also costs a draw call per UI element.

- At world load, every non-TMP `Graphic` (Image, RawImage) whose GameObject is inactive in the uploaded scene has its `material` replaced with a new material named `VRChat/Mobile/Worlds/Supersampled UI`. That's one new material per Graphic.

- It happens even when the Graphic already uses `VRCSuperSampledUIMaterial`.

- Graphics that are active at load keep the shared material. Toggling objects off and on later never triggers it.

- The swap happens at load: the material is already replaced while the object is still inactive.

- Udon isn't involved. A script-free copy of the UI reproduces it.

Every affected element has a unique material, so the canvas can't batch it. One of our menu pages draws 92 batches instead of 12. Any world that keeps pages, menus or row templates disabled until needed pays this on every hidden element. In our world that's about 2,100 UI graphics.

1. Make a world-space canvas with a few Images using `VRCSuperSampledUIMaterial`, then duplicate it.

2. Set the duplicate's root inactive, then Build & Test.

3. In the client, enable the inactive copy.

4. Log `material.name` and `material.GetInstanceID()` for each Image (from Udon). The always-active copy shares the asset material. The late copy has a separate runtime material per Image, all named `VRChat/Mobile/Worlds/Supersampled UI`.

Expected:

The auto-swap only touches `UI/Default` (as the 2023.4.2 notes describe). Where it does swap, Graphics share one material instead of getting one each.

Workaround:

Reassigning the original material from Udon after load (`graphic.material = sharedMaterial`) restores batching, and it sticks through later toggles.
title: Supersampled UI auto-swap gives every UI Graphic that is inactive at world load its own material (breaks UI batching)
